A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REOrder work. The complete 17-page v1 and 20-page v2, including Appendices A–H, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-1K and FMoW classification experiments, patch-order comparisons, REOrder results, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds longer-training experiments, permutation controls, and quantitative patch-position analysis.

M1.justification: The compression-based initialization, Plackett-Luce policy, REINFORCE objective, Gumbel sampling, training curriculum, and deterministic inference remain unchanged. Additional parameter and schedule descriptions document the existing procedure; per-image ordering is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: The reported classification benchmarks remain ImageNet-1K and FMoW. Appendix A newly states that experiments using 5888×5888 images have been initiated, extending the reported scope to an ultra-high-resolution input scenario. These experiments are explicitly ongoing and have no reported outcomes.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2/Table 4 adds fixed-random and fixed-final-learned permutations as comparators for Transformer-XL on ImageNet-1K. Random permutations sampled per batch already appeared in v1 Appendix A. The backbone set and six standard patch orders remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds continuation from 100 to 300 epochs for row-major Transformer-XL with and without REOrder. Appendix D.2 adds controls using fixed random or previously learned permutations throughout training. These are limited extensions of the evaluation design; the principal splits, metrics, and training recipe remain.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens tests of the proposed mechanism through longer training, static-random and static-learned ordering controls, and quantitative central-patch displacement analysis in Appendix H. These address optimization duration and the contribution of policy-driven exploration. The existing no-flip ablation is retained as D.3/Table 5, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions estimate SEM using 2,000 nonparametric bootstrap resamples. v2 clarifies several uncertainty units as percentage points but introduces no new repeated-seed reporting, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test. The three additional permutation runs represent different conditions, not repeated seeds.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 add longer-training and control outcomes, including 53.10% for fixed-random, 50.23% for per-batch-random, and 53.07% for fixed-learned ordering. Appendix H adds mean patch-position shifts. Figure 3 changes FMoW correlations from 0.67 to 0.24 for Mamba and -0.95 to -0.92 for ViT. Figure 5's principal REOrder results remain unchanged. Some new numerical reports are internally unreconciled.

T1.justification: The permutation-equivariance proposition and proof, policy probability equations, and formal rasterization definitions remain substantively unchanged. The variable-name typo introduced after Appendix B's Equation 5 does not constitute a new assumption or mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: patch-order sensitivity and the two-stage REOrder framework. The headline reported gains of 3.01% on ImageNet-1K and 13.35% on FMoW are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving ARM's directional processing and image anisotropy, architectural differences in central-patch positioning, and the necessity of guided exploration rather than merely reusing a learned order. It also explicitly identifies the shared global permutation as a limitation and expands discussion of compression's limited predictive value and unresolved long-sequence scalability.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly supplies Transformer-XL memory length 128, Longformer window size 14, a 15-epoch policy warm-up, triangular temperature scheduling with peak 0.2, and the 196-parameter policy size. These are disclosures, not established implementation changes. The newly stated policy learning rate of 1e-4 is not reconciled with the retained general RL rate of 1e-5. Code and data access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 24 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Expanded explanations of the selected architectures do not materially change novelty claims or positioning against prior research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introductory edits, expands model and curriculum explanations, rewrites interpretive passages, and adds appendix subsections and cross-references. The main section sequence and Appendix A–H organization remain intact; most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–4, renumbers the unchanged no-flip table to Table 5, revises Figures 2–3 axes and tick formatting, and expands Figure 4's caption. Figure 2's FMoW axis contracts from approximately ±7 to ±2.4, and its Mamba bars are no longer visible. Other figure artwork and the overall layout style are retained.

improvement.justification: The added controls, implementation details, and explicit limitations are useful. However, the new evidence has unresolved reporting problems: D.1 reports 61.20% versus 60.80%, inconsistent with Table 3's +1.19-point increase; Table 4 reports 50.23% for per-batch randomness while Appendix A retains 39.07% without distinguishing conditions. Figure 2 also loses visible FMoW Mamba bars. These benefits and reporting regressions prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
